samples:
What, if anything, can a person be completely certain of?
nothing_at_all / yes_many_things / only_logic_and_math / only_my_own_existence

What is the best sign that someone is a good thinker?
they_are_consistent / they_know_many_facts / they_admit_uncertainty / they_change_their_mind / they_ask_good_questions

Which is the most common reason smart people believe false things?
overconfidence / they_rarely_do / lack_of_information / motivated_reasoning / trusting_the_wrong_people

What is the right attitude toward a belief you've held since childhood?
doubt_it_by_default / keep_it_until_disproven / re_examine_it_from_time_to_time

How much can people ever know about the world beyond their senses?
Nothing / Very little / A good deal / Almost everything, in principle

How much do you trust your own memory of events from years ago?
Not at all / Only the broad outline / Most details / Every detail

How much of what you currently believe do you expect will turn out to be wrong?
None of it / A few small things / A fair share / Much of it

How willing are you to say you're certain about something?
Never / Only for logic and math / For well-established facts / For most things I believe
Is absolute certainty ever justified?
Is intuition a reliable guide to truth?
Should you believe something just because most experts agree?
Have you changed your mind about something important in the last year?

child.label: Knowledge & Certainty
child.description: Questions about what knowledge is, whether certainty is possible, and the answerer's own habits of doubt, confidence, and changing their mind.
child.not_for: Which kinds of evidence, sources, experts, or media to trust (use Evidence & Sources).
examples: Can a false belief still be useful?

samples:
When someone presents strong evidence against a belief you hold, what do you usually do?
keep_my_belief / change_it_slowly / change_my_mind_right_away / look_for_counter_evidence

How much weight does a famous scientist's opinion deserve on a topic outside their specialty?
less_than_a_layperson / no_more_than_a_layperson / as_much_as_in_their_field / a_little_more_than_a_layperson

When your gut feeling and the evidence disagree, which do you follow?
evidence / gut_feeling / depends_on_the_stakes / look_for_more_information

What is the most reliable source of knowledge?
trusted_people / expert_consensus / scientific_studies / personal_experience / reasoning_it_out_myself

Which is worse: believing something false or failing to believe something true?
equally_bad / missing_something_true / believing_something_false

What should you do when experts disagree with each other?
suspend_judgment / follow_the_majority / look_at_the_evidence_myself / follow_the_most_credentialed

How should you treat a claim you read on social media?
assume_its_false / check_the_source / look_for_other_sources / believe_it_if_it_seems_right

Which kind of evidence convinces you most?
statistics / a_vivid_story / a_trusted_person / seeing_it_myself / a_logical_argument

What is the best response to a belief that can't be tested?
ignore_it / reject_it / hold_it_lightly / believe_it_if_it_helps

Which is more trustworthy?
an_ai_system / a_single_expert / my_own_judgment / a_large_crowd_of_non_experts

What should you do if a well-supported scientific finding clashes with your experience?
hold_both / trust_the_science / trust_my_experience / look_into_it_further

What makes a source trustworthy to you?
credentials / independence / track_record / agrees_with_what_i_know / transparency_about_methods

child.label: Evidence & Sources
child.description: Questions about which evidence, sources, experts, statistics, news, or gut feelings to trust when deciding whether a claim is true.
child.not_for: What knowledge is, whether anything is certain, and personal habits of doubt (use Knowledge & Certainty).
examples: Do you trust a vivid story more than a statistic?
Should you follow the experts when they disagree with your gut?
